claim: Build keeps one open span per screen column. When a building's walls are low enough to see over, the columns above them stay open for what is behind, and anything the renderer reaches through a door in that wall paints into them too: an open door into a roofed room smeared 18,000 to 23,000 pixels of its ceiling across the sky over the facade.
evidence: seen in the XMapEdit observer run of experiments/church-roofs (README there); the owner saw the matching lid of a low sky walking it in NBlood, 2026-11-17
projects/blood-city/level/l3_church.py: the church is entered only through its tower, whose walls close every column they cover

measured in the observer (JFBuild's classic renderer, not NBlood's default renderer): porch under the roof with the door shut 395 to 3,970 px across nine frames, door open 6,960 to 23,262; entrance through the tower with its doors shut 0 (experiments/church-roofs measurements.txt; tests/test_skyline.py LeakTests)
self-closing doors (doors.z_motion_door(close_after=30)) only mitigate: with both held open the leak is there
use: Enter a building that is seen over through a part nothing is seen over (a tower, a porch with its own tall sky), or through two doors that are never open together; bloodmap.skyline checks it on the source. skyline.leaks_under_roofs(layout) finds the violating doors on the source.
